title: Thousands march in Bordeaux against cost of living and for public services
seoTitle: Bordeaux march against cost of living

tea.why: Protesters marched against the rising cost of living, lower pensions, and in support of youth and public services like education and health.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded better purchasing power, ecological transition, generational justice, and improved conditions for public services and students.
tea.changed: Nov 5: A large demonstration took place in Bordeaux drawing thousands of participants, followed by late clashes with law enforcement.

summary: On November 5, 2026, a large demonstration took place in Bordeaux, France, as part of a general strike day against the cost of living and in defense of public services. Initiated by trade union coalitions including the CGT, FSU, and FO, and heavily supported by students, teachers, and healthcare workers, the march brought together diverse groups of citizens, including retirees and first-time participants. According to the prefecture, 21,000 people participated, while organizers from the CGT estimated the crowd at 120,000. While the main march initially proceeded in a calm atmosphere along a route bypassing the hypercenter, clashes with security forces broke out more than an hour after the gathering ended at Place de la Victoire.
demands: Support for youth and student demands
response: According to sources, authorities validated a specific march route avoiding the hypercenter to protect businesses, and reported that clashes with law enforcement occurred more than an hour after the demonstration concluded at Place de la Victoire.

updates.text: Thousands marched through Bordeaux for a general strike day against the cost of living.
Clashes between individuals and law enforcement occurred after the demonstration concluded at Place de la Victoire.
Authorities announced a subsequent authorized march scheduled for Saturday, November 7.
